verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              तथा गतेषु शूरेषु तेषां मम च सञ्जय। किं वै भीमस्तदाऽकार्षीत्तन्ममाचक्ष्व सञ्जय॥१॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said When the warriors on their side and mine remained thus on the field of battle, what did Bhima do? Tell me, this O Sanjaya.

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              विरथो भीमसेनो वै कर्णवाक्शल्यपीडितः। अमर्षवशमापन्नः फाल्गुनं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥२॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said When Bhimasena was made carless by Karna, he was tormented with the words poignant as a dart, of the latter. Now under the influence of passion he said these words of Phalguna.

verses.sanskrit: पुनः पुनस्तूबरक मूढ औदरिकेति च। अकृतास्त्रक मा योत्सीर्बाल संग्रामकातर॥३॥
इति मामब्रवीत्कर्णः पश्यतस्ते धनञ्जय। एवं वक्ता च मे वध्यस्तेन चोक्तोऽस्मि भारत॥४॥
verses.english: "O Dhananjaya, in your very presence, Karna has repeatedly said to me-(you are) a eunuch, fool, child, glutton, (you are) unable to endure (the fury of) battle. He, that would tell me so, would be my victim. O Bharata, he (Karna) has said to me these words (and therefore, he must be slain by me),

verses.sanskrit: एतद्व्रतं महाबाहो त्वया सह कृतं मया। तथैतन्मम कौन्तेय यथा तव न संशयः॥५॥
verses.english: I have made this vow jointly with you, O mighty armed one. O son of Kunti undoubtedly, as they (these vows) are to you so they are to me.

verses.sanskrit: तद्वधाय नरश्रेष्ठ स्मरैतद्वचनं मम। यथा भवति तत्सत्यं तथा कुरु धनञ्जय॥६॥
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य भीमस्यामितविक्रमः। ततोऽर्जुनोऽब्रवीत्कर्णं किंचिदभ्येत्य संयुगे॥७॥
verses.english: Thus addressed by Bhima, Arjuna of matchless prowess, coming up to Karna in that battle, said to him (thus):

verses.sanskrit: कर्ण कर्ण वृथादृष्टे सूतपुत्रात्मसंस्तुत। अधर्मबुद्धे शृणु मे यत्त्वां वक्ष्यामि सांप्रतम्॥८॥
द्विविधं कर्म शूराणां युद्धे जयपराजयौ। तौ चाप्यनित्यौ राधेय वासवस्यापि युध्यतः॥९॥
verses.english: Warriors either meet with victory or defeat in battle. O son of Radha, even these two are uncertain. Even when Vasava himself fights, the case is not otherwise.

verses.sanskrit: मुमूर्षुर्युयुधानेन विरथो विकलेन्द्रियः। मद्वध्यस्त्वमिति ज्ञात्वा जित्वा जीवन्विसर्जितः॥१०॥
यदृच्छया रणे भीमं युध्यमानं महाबलम्। कथञ्चिद्विरथं कृत्वा यत्त्वं रूक्षमभाषथाः॥११॥
अधर्मस्त्वेष सुमहाननार्यचरितं च तत्। नारिं जित्वाऽतिकत्थन्ते न च जल्पन्ति दुर्वचः॥१२॥
verses.english: Men, that are heroic, virtuous and most exalted, having defeated an enemy, neither! boast of themselves with harsh words, nor indulge in abusive language.

verses.sanskrit: न च कञ्चन निन्दन्ति सन्तः शूरा नरर्षभाः। त्वं तु प्राकृतविज्ञानस्वत्तद्वदसि सूतज॥१३॥
verses.english: O son of a charioteer, weak in intellect as you are, you have made use of these words. Again, the (abusive) epithets that you have hurled against the fighting Bhimasena, endued with prowess, heroic and ever devoted to righteousness, are not true. In the very sight of the whole army of Keshava and myself.

verses.sanskrit: बह्वबद्धमकर्ण्यं च चापलादपरीक्षितम्। युध्यमानं पराक्रान्तं शूरमार्यव्रते रतम्॥१४॥
यदवोचोऽप्रियं भीमं नैतत्सत्यं वचस्तव। पश्यतां सर्वसैन्यानां केशवस्य ममैव च॥१५॥
विरथो भीमसेनेन कृतोऽसि बहुशो रणे। न च त्वां परुषं किञ्चिदुक्तवान्पाण्डुनन्दनः॥१६॥
verses.english: You were several times, in battle, deprived of your car by Bhimasena. But the son of Pandu did never utter any harsh words to you.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मात्तु बहु रूक्षं च श्रावितस्ते वृकोदरः। परोक्षं यच्च सौभद्रो युष्माभिर्निहतो मम॥१७॥
तस्मादस्यावलेपस्य सद्यः फलमवाप्नुहि। त्वया तस्य धनुश्छिन्नमात्मनाशाय दुर्मते॥१८॥
verses.english: You will, therefore, very soon feel the consequences of your offense. () wicked minded one, it was for your own destruction that you cut-off his bow.

verses.sanskrit: तस्माद्वध्योऽसि मे मूढ सभृत्य-सुत-बान्धवः। कुरु त्वं सर्वकृत्यानि महत् ते भयमागतम्॥१९॥
verses.english: It is for this reason, O fool, that I will slay you together with your attendants, forces and beast of burden. Now (while yet there is time) perform what you ought to do, because a great calamity is hanging over you.

verses.sanskrit: हन्तास्मि वृषसेनं ते प्रेक्षमाणस्य संयुगे। ये चान्येप्युपयास्यन्ति बुद्धिमोहेन मां नृपाः॥२०॥
तांश्च सर्वान्हनिष्यामि सत्येनायुधमालभे। त्वां च मूढा कृतप्रज्ञमतिमानिनमाहवे॥२१॥
verses.english: I swear truly by my bow that I will slay, in your very sight, Vrishasena and will destroy all those other kings, who through cloudiness of intellect will oppose me in battle. Fool, unwise and self-conceited that you are, the wicked Duryodhana will give way to lamentations seeing you slain on the field of battle. Arjuna having promised to kill the son of Karna.
verses.bhavadeepa: वृषसेनं ते तव पुत्रमिति शेषः । बुद्धिमोहेन बुद्धिविभ्रमेण ॥२०॥

verses.sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनो मन्दो भृशं तप्स्यति पातितम्। अर्जुनेन प्रतिज्ञाते वधे कर्णसुतस्य तु॥२२॥
महान्सुतुमुलः शब्दो बभूव रथिनां तदा। तस्मिन्नाकुलसंग्रामे वर्तमाने महाभये॥२३॥
verses.english: There arose a great and tumultuous uproar among the car-warriors. And at the time of that dreadful battle.

verses.sanskrit: मन्दरश्मिः सहस्रांशुरस्तं गिरिमुपाद्रवत्। ततो राजन्हृषीकेशः संग्रामशिरसि स्थितम्॥२४॥
verses.english: The thousand-rayed (deity) with his rays dimmed entered into the setting hill. Then stationed at the head of the battle, O king, Hrishikesa.

verses.sanskrit: तीर्णप्रतिज्ञं बीभत्सुं परिष्वज्यैनमब्रवीत्। दिष्ट्या संपादिता जिष्णो प्रतिज्ञा महती त्वया॥२५॥
verses.english: Embraced Vibhatsu, who had fulfilled his promise and addressed him thus-"O Jishnu, it is by good fortune that you have been able to accomplish your great vow.

verses.sanskrit: दिष्ट्या विनिहतः पापो वृद्धक्षत्रः सहात्मजः। धार्तराष्ट्रबलं प्राप्य देवसेनापि भारत॥२६॥
verses.english: It is by good luck, again that you have slain the wretch Vridhakshatra together with his son. O Bharata, even the general of the celestials, if engaged with the force of Dhritarashtra.

verses.sanskrit: सीदेत समरे जिष्णो नात्र कार्या विचारणा। न तं पश्यामि लोकेषु चिन्तयन्पुरुषं क्वचित्॥२७॥
verses.english: In battle, would be quite stupefied. O Jishnu, there is no doubt of this. Even on reflection, I do not find any individual in the (three) words.

verses.sanskrit: त्वदृते पुरुषव्याघ्र य एतद्योधयेद्बलम्। महाप्रभावा बहवस्त्वया तुल्याधिकाऽपि वा॥२८॥
verses.english: Capable of encountering these forces, besides you, O most valiant of men. Numerous lords of the earth, endowed with great prowess and either equal or superior to you, have, at the command of Dhritarashtra assembled together. (But) those (warriors). clad in armour, could not withstand your wrathful self in battle.

verses.sanskrit: समेताः पृथिवीपाला धार्तराष्ट्रस्य कारणात्। ते त्वां प्राप्य रणे क्रुद्धा नाभ्यवर्तन्त दंशिताः॥२९॥
तव वीर्यं बलं चैव रुद्रशकान्तकोपमम्। नेदृशं शक्नुयात्कश्चिद्रणे कर्तुं पराक्रमम्॥३०॥
verses.english: Your strength and prowess, (therefore), resemble those of Rudra or Shakra. No one is capable of displaying so much prowess in battle.

verses.sanskrit: यादृशं कृतवानद्य त्वमेकः शत्रुतापनः। एवमेव हते कर्णे सानुबन्धे दुरात्मनि॥३१॥
verses.english: As you have singly shown this day. O tormentor of foes, when the wicked-souled Karna together with his followers shall be vanquished (by you) I will thus.

verses.sanskrit: वर्धयिष्यामि भूयस्त्वां विजितारिं हतद्विषम्। तमर्जुनः प्रत्युवाच प्रसादात्तव माधव॥३२॥
verses.english: o destroyer of Madhu, you are (ever) concerned in our welfare and we are always) at your enemy." Arjuna then replied to him (thus)-"O Madhava, through your favour, I have fulfilled the vow, which even by the celestials can with difficulty be performed. O Keshava, it is no wonder that they, who have you for their lord, will win the victory. Through your favour Yudhishthira will recover the entire earth. O descendant of Vrishnis, (as) all this is due to your power, (so) O lord, this victory is yours. O destroyer of Madhu, you are (ever) concerned in our welfare wand we are (always) at your service.” Thus spoken to Krishna with a smile, slowly guided the steeds and showed to Partha the greatly cruel field of battle.

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिज्ञेयं मया तीर्णा विबुधैरपि दुस्तरा। अनाश्चर्यो जयस्तेषां येषां नाथोऽसि केशव॥३३॥
त्वत्प्रसादान्महीं कृत्स्नां संप्राप्स्यति युधिष्ठिरः। तव प्रभावो वार्ष्णेय तवैव विजयः प्रभो॥३४॥
वर्धनीयास्तव वयं सदैव मधुसूदन। एवमुक्तस्ततः कृष्णः शनकैर्वाहयन्हयान्॥३५॥

दर्शयामास पार्थाय क्रूरमायोधनं महत्।
              श्रीकृष्ण उवाच।
              प्रार्थयन्तो जयं युद्धे प्रथितं च महद्यशः॥३६॥
verses.english: Krishna said Longing for either victory or great renown, (many) heroic kings, struck dead by your shafts, are lying on earth.

verses.sanskrit: पृथिव्यां शेरते शूराः पार्थिवास्त्वच्छरैर्हताः। विकीर्णशस्त्राभरणा विपन्नाश्व-रथ-द्विपाः। संछिन्नभिन्नमर्माणो वैक्लव्यं परमं गताः॥३७॥
verses.english: Their weapons and ornaments lie scattered (all over the battle-field); their horses, elephants and cars are killed and shattered; and with their armour perforated and cut-off they are reduced to a woeful plight.

verses.sanskrit: ससत्त्वा गतसत्त्वाश्च प्रभया परया युताः। सजीवा इव लक्ष्यन्ते गतसत्त्वा नराधिपाः॥३८॥
तेषां शरैः स्वर्णपुंखैः शस्त्रैश्च विविधैः शितैः। वाहनैरायुधैश्चैव संपूर्णां पश्य मेदिनीम्॥३९॥
वर्मभिश्चर्मभिर्हारैः शिरोभिश्च सकुण्डलैः। उष्णीषैर्मुकुटैः स्रग्भिश्चूडामणिभिरम्बरैः॥४०॥
verses.english: (Behold) O Bharata, the earth became with armours, necklaces of gold, heads decked with ear-rings, head-gears and diadems, floral wreaths, gems worn on the crown, Kanthasutras, Angadas, lustrous collars of gold and with various other variegated ornaments;

verses.sanskrit: कण्ठसूत्रैरङ्गदैश्च निष्कैरपि च सप्रभैः। अन्यैश्चाभरणैश्चित्रैर्भाति भारत मेदिनी॥४१॥
अनुकर्षैरुपासङ्गैः पताकाभिर्ध्वजैस्तथा। उपस्करैरधिष्ठानैरीषादण्डकबन्धुरैः॥४२॥
चक्रैः प्रमथितश्चित्रैरक्षैश्च बहुधा रणे। युगैर्योक्तैः कलापैश्च धनुर्भिः सायकैस्तथा॥४३॥
verses.english: With broken wheels and many variegated cars, yokes and trappings of horses, bow and arrows.

verses.sanskrit: परिस्तोमैः कुथाभिश्च परिघैरङ्कुशैस्तथा। शक्तिभिर्भिन्दिपालैश्च तूर्णैः शूलैः परश्वधैः॥४४॥
verses.english: With elephants' trappings, Kudhas, Parighas and Ankushas, maces and Brindipalas, arrow-cases, spiked maces and Parasvadhas.

verses.sanskrit: प्रासैश्च तोमरैश्चैव कुन्तैर्यष्टिभिरेव च। शतघ्नीभिर्भुशुण्डीभिः खड्गैः परशुभिस्तथा॥४५॥
verses.english: With Pashas and Tomaras, Kuntas and clubs, Sataghness and Bhusandees, swords and battle-axes.

verses.sanskrit: मुसलैर्मुद्गरैश्चैव गदाभिः कुणपैस्तथा। सुवर्णविकृताभिश्च कशाभिर्भरतर्षभ॥४६॥
घण्टाभिश्च गजेन्द्राणां भाण्डैश्च विविधैरपि। स्रग्भिश्च नानाभरणैर्वस्त्रैश्चैव महाधनैः॥४७॥
verses.english: With the bells and many other ornaments of the best of elephants, garlands, various ornaments and costly dresses.

verses.sanskrit: अपविद्धैर्बभौ भूमिर्गृहैर्द्यौरिव शारदी। पृथिव्यां पृथिवीहेतोः पृथिवीपतयो हताः॥४८॥
verses.english: (With all these lying scattered all over the field of battle), the earth looks resplendent like the autumnal sky studded with planets and stars. Those lords of Earth who have sacrificed their live for his sake.

verses.sanskrit: पृथिवीमुपगुह्याङ्गैः सुप्ताः कान्तामिव प्रियाम्। इमांश्च गिरिकूटाभान्नागानैरावतोपमान्॥४९॥
verses.english: Lie slumbering on the earth and embracing her like a beloved wife. These elephants resembling mountain-peaks and huge Airavat.

verses.sanskrit: क्षरतः शोणितं भूरि शस्त्रच्छेददरीमुखैः। दरीमुखैरिव गिरीन् गैरिकांबुपरिस्रवान्॥५०॥
verses.english: Are shedding a profusion of blood through the openings caused by weapons, as mountains discharge through the caves streams of liquid chalk.

verses.sanskrit: तांश्च बाणहतान्वीर पश्य निष्टनतः क्षितौ। हयांश्च पतितान्पश्य स्वर्णभाण्डविभूषितान्॥५१॥
गन्धर्वनगराकारान् रथांश्च निहतेश्वरान्। छिन्नध्वजपताकाक्षान्विचक्रान्हतसारथीन्॥५२॥
verses.english: Behold, O Partha, O lord, these cars resembling the city of the Gandharvas, with their lords slain and their standards, banners and Akshas cut to pieces, deprived of their wheels and charioteers, with their yokes cut to pieces, with broken shafts and crests and looking (splendid) like the celestial vehicles.

verses.sanskrit: निकृत्तकूबरयुगान्भग्नेषान्बन्धुरान्प्रभो। पश्य पार्थ हयान्भूमौ विमानोपमदर्शनान्॥५३॥
पतींश्च निहतान्वीर शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। धनुर्भृतश्चर्मभृतः शयानान् रुधिरोक्षितान्॥५४॥
verses.english: Hundreds and thousands of foot-soldiers, O hero, are lying slain (on the ground) in a pool of blood wielding their bows and shields.

verses.sanskrit: महीमालिंग्य सर्वाङ्गैः पांसुध्वस्तशिरोरुहान्। पश्य योधान्महाबाहो त्वच्छरैर्भिन्नविग्रहान्॥५५॥
verses.english: Clasping the earth with all their limbs and with their hair smeared with dust. Behold, O mighty-armed one, these warriors with their bodies mangled by your arrows.

verses.sanskrit: निपातितद्विप-रथ-वाजिसंकुल-मसृग्वसा-पिशितसमृद्धकर्दमम्। निशाचर-श्व-वृक-पिशाचमोदनं महीतलं नरवर पश्य दुर्द्दशम्॥५६॥
verses.english: O best of men, behold also the surface of the earth with dead elephants and horses and (broken) cars, muddy with a profusion of blood, fat and rotten flesh, affording delight to night of blood, fat the rotten flesh, affording delight to night-wanderers, dogs, wolves and Pisachas and dreadful to look at.

verses.sanskrit: इदं महत्त्वय्युपपद्यते प्रभो रणाजिरे कर्म यशोभिवर्धनम्। शतक्रतौ चापि च देवसत्तमे महाहवे जघ्नुषि दैत्यदानवान्॥५७॥
verses.english: O lord, that foremost of the celestials, the performer of a hundred sacrifices who slay in great battle the Daytas and the Danavas and yourself only are capable of achieving such a fame-enhancing and glorious feat.

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              एवं सन्दर्शयन् कृष्णो रणभूमिं किरीटिने। स्वैः समेतः समुदितैः पाञ्चजन्यं व्यनादयत्॥५८॥
verses.english: Janardana, the destroyer of foes, having (thus) shown to Kiriti the field of battle, speedily came over to the Pandavas Ajatastru (i.e., Yudhishthira who had no enemy) and informed him of destruction of Jayadratha.

verses.sanskrit: स दर्शयन्नेव किरीटिनेऽरिहा जनार्दनस्तामरिभूमिमञ्जसा। अजातशत्रुं समुपेत्य पाण्डवं निवेदयामास हतं जयद्रथम्॥५८॥
verses.english: Janardana, the destroyer of foes, having (thus) shown to Kiriti the field of battle, speedily came over to the Pandavas Ajatastru (i.e., Yudhishthira who had no enemy) and informed him of destruction of Jayadratha.
